gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of its five picks will run or charge from a USB-C power bank and the minimum bank output each maker sets: the MoGo 4 needs a 65–150 W USB-C PD source, the Capsule 3 needs at least 45 W PD2.0 at 5–20 V, the MoGo 2 Pro has no battery and needs a USB-C PD source of at least 65 W, and the Vibe One has no USB-C power input, only a DC barrel jack.
standout_why: I compared against all three cited pages. The Hook Up's 'Read BEFORE You Buy a Portable Projector in 2026' covers power input for the Elfin Flip Plus (DC barrel jack, 20 V USB-C-to-barrel adapter, 90 minutes on a 20,000 mAh bank). It doesn't cover the MoGo 4, Capsule 3, MoGo 2 Pro or Vibe One, so it has no minimum bank wattage for any of ChatGPT's other picks. The two RTINGS pages (best under $500, best portable) loaded only menus and no pick text, so I couldn't read their power-input coverage. ChatGPT's answer says only 'Battery' or 'Requires external power'. It gives no wattage floor and never says the Vibe One lacks USB-C power.
decides: This is a tiebreaker within ChatGPT's 'portable with battery' slot rather than a full reversal. A shopper who wants to extend runtime with a 45 W bank they already own should get the Capsule 3: Nebula accepts 45 W, while the MoGo 4 needs at least 65 W. The MoGo 2 Pro ($359 in ChatGPT's answer) only works off the wall if the source is a USB-C PD power bank of at least 65 W. SlashGear found it would not run from a 65 W laptop wall plug. For the Vibe One, ChatGPT's 'Budget-friendly, easy to move around' lacks a caveat: it can't be topped up over USB-C without a third-party DC-to-USB-C cable. That weakens it as a travel pick next to the Capsule 3 and MoGo 4. The MoGo 4 remains the pick for runtime (71.28 Wh, 2.5 h in Eco mode), but the bank you pair it with must be rated 65 W or higher.

findings.label: Power source requirement
findings.value: No internal battery; USB-C power input; runs off a battery pack giving 65 W or more; drew about 40 W
findings.source_title: Xgimi Mogo 2 Pro Review: A Smaller, Lighter, And Cheaper Smart Projector – SlashGear
findings.note: Adam Doud (SlashGear, 2023-04-26) ran it from an Anker 737 24,000 mAh pack and estimated about 2 h 15 min at about 40 W. He reports it 'will not run off of a wall plug that outputs at 65W' (tested with a 65 W laptop charger versus an Anker 737 120 W plug). Other reviews in search results disagree on the 65 W wall plug, and I could not open the maker page to settle it.
